quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Speed up gradually as you exit. Speeding up when entering a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines generally cannot. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, what must you do?

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: Which traffic light means: stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe?
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the side with the broken line.
You can pass from the side with the solid line.
No one can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the lane next to the broken line.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to where you came from.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to where you came from.

questions.question: What do round signs warn you about?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings ahead.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you that a railroad crossing is coming. Be extra careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT safe for night driving?

options.text: Know that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Do not look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles. This will cause your eyes to adjust to the bright light. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to readjust, leaving you nearly blind during that period.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight ahead down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded. This lets you see the road and stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: Two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left can go when it is safe.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn loudly.
questions.explanation: Honk your horn loudly when a child or other pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your vehicle. This warns them of danger.

questions.question: A driver license is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it by following the rules.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn at this location.

questions.question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way, even if you signal your turn.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass:

options.text: If you are on an expressway.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: You can cross the broken yellow line to pass if no traffic is coming toward you.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns you that a sharp turn is coming. You should slow down.

questions.question: Your vehicle wheels have gone off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, and brake gently. Slowing down safely lets you find a good place to get back on the road. Turning the wheel sharply can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: When you are ready to turn left from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the center line.
questions.explanation: Position your car near the center line when turning left from a two-way street. Turn when the front of your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut corners.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns you that the space ahead is too low for tall vehicles. Watch for overhead obstacles.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. Children are playing nearby. Before you move, you should:

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing up. Mirrors alone are not enough, especially when children are nearby.

questions.question: Alcohol is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has many turns or curves.

questions.question: To avoid glare from the headlights of an approaching car:

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Stay focused on the centerline on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights of an oncoming vehicle. Then look ahead to see where the other car is.

questions.question: When a stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, a driver:

options.text: Is required to slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
Should stop only at a place where they can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if they have to enter the intersecting roadway.
Should stop where they have a clear view of approaching traffic before they enter the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should stop where they have a clear view of approaching traffic before they enter the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle when using a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk at any time because it is the vehicle driver's responsibility to stop.
Use crosswalks only if they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a nearby vehicle may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed in every location where there is a present danger.
Indicate what a driver must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn drivers that they are approaching a school zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Indicate what a driver must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black text. They tell drivers what they must or must not do, such as speed limits or no-passing zones.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping:

options.text: On a wet or icy road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: To be able to turn quickly, your hands must be:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position helps you turn quickly and safely on high-speed roads.

questions.question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, drivers should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Yield whenever it helps prevent collisions.
